- Updated API domain in skill metadata from agent-api-dev.aicoding.live to agent-api.sparki.io
- No user-facing command or flow changes
- Internal metadata adjustment to production API endpoint

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement a legitimate Sparki video-editing CLI and only needs an API key and local file access, but there are inconsistencies in the packaging/installation metadata and a narrow declared network allowance that doesn't fully reflect the code's behavior — review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the code and instructions: CLI uploads local video files or uses a Telegram upload link and calls Sparki backend endpoints. Requiring SPARKI_API_KEY, reading local files, and writing outputs to ~/.openclaw/workspace/sparki are all reasonable for a video-editing skill. Requiring the 'uv' binary (used to 'uv sync') is plausible as the project's chosen sync/install mechanism.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to validate the API key, return a Telegram upload link, accept local file paths, and run upload/edit/status/download commands — all consistent with the stated purpose. It explicitly tells the agent to read local files and write to the configured workspace, which is expected. It also instructs proactive use when video-editing is mentioned; combined with autonomous invocation this could lead to the skill being triggered more often than users expect (autonomy itself is platform-default).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata reported 'No install spec — instruction-only', but SKILL.md contains an 'install' entry and the bundle includes scripts/setup.sh that runs 'uv sync'. This mismatch between the registry summary and the included files is an inconsistency you should verify. The install flow relies on 'uv' (linked in setup.sh to https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh), which is an external installer; fetching/executing that script has the usual risks if you do not trust the source.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The only declared primary credential is SPARKI_API_KEY (appropriate for a hosted API). The code also supports an optional SPARKI_UPLOAD_TG_LINK and stores config in ~/.openclaw; nothing asks for unrelated credentials or broad secret access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always: false. The skill writes its own config and a local history file under the user's ~/.openclaw directory, which is expected for a CLI tool. It does not request global or other-skill configuration changes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill mostly behaves like an expected CLI client for Sparki, but check a few things before installing: 1) The package metadata claims 'instruction-only' but the bundle contains code and a setup script — prefer to install only if you trust the source. 2) The install uses the 'uv' tool (setup.sh points users to an external installer at astral.sh); review that installer before running it. 3) The SKILL.md/network metadata lists only agent-api.sparki.io, but the CLI will download result URLs returned by the API (which could redirect to CDNs or third-party hosts); if you want strict network controls, verify where result URLs originate. 4) The skill will read local video files and write outputs to ~/.openclaw/workspace/sparki and a local history file; run in a sandbox if you are cautious. If you cannot verify the origin of the bundle or the safety of the 'uv' installer, do not install or run it with sensitive credentials.
